title: Tidier scan review
bullets: The text that says a line matched an entry is now easy to read.
The scan review no longer has an important switch. You can still mark an entry important from the entry itself.

title: Apply works on monthly log scans
bullets: Apply now works when you scan a monthly log.
A line with no day starts unticked, so it no longer blocks the rest.

title: Scanning keeps indented lines
bullets: Scanning keeps indented lines under the line above, like notes under a meeting.
In the scan review you can nest or un-nest a line if the guess is wrong.

title: Monthly and future log reminders
bullets: After you migrate, a nudge offers to open the monthly log.
On the first open of a new month, a nudge offers to open the future log.
Both can be dismissed with Not now.

title: Scan a page or note again
bullets: A scanned note that looks like a saved one can update it instead of making a copy.
Scan again on a note reads the page once more into that note.
Scan this page again on a day updates that day's entries.

title: Scan offer once everything is on paper
bullets: When you mark the last entry as written, the list offers to scan the page. Tap Not now to skip it.

title: Swiping keeps the rows in place
bullets: Swiping an entry no longer nudges the rows around it; every row stays on its grid line.

title: Scan reads struck-through tasks
bullets: A task struck through on paper shows up in the scan review as dropped, and you can change it there.
Applying the scan marks it dropped; nothing is deleted.

title: Older open tasks reach the review
bullets: The migration review now offers every open task from earlier days, however long ago, not just the last week.

title: "not synced" stays in one piece
bullets: The quiet "not synced" mark no longer splits across lines, and its dots stay right next to it.

title: Wrapped rows stay on the dot grid
bullets: Long titles that run over two or more lines now end on the dots, so every row below keeps its place.

title: Long titles stay visible when you swipe
bullets: Swipe a task to move it and the whole title stays on screen, even when it runs over several lines.

title: Mark important from the edit sheet
bullets: Mark or unmark an entry as important in its edit sheet, and on a line in the scan review. The * still means the same thing.

title: Rename or delete a collection
bullets: Open a collection in Notes to rename it, or to delete the page. Its entries are not deleted: they stay in the log.

title: A little less air between lines
bullets: Wrapped lines sit a little closer than yesterday, still with more room than before.

title: Add a task to a note
bullets: Press and hold a task's dot in the log and tap Note to add the task as a new line at the end of a note. The task then leaves the log.

title: More room between lines
bullets: Entries that wrap onto a second or third line now have more air between the lines.

title: Notes you write, and collections
bullets: The Notes tab has a New note button: write a note of several lines by hand, no scan needed. It keeps its title and day, and sits on the grid next to your scanned notes.

A collection is a named page, like books to read. Tap New collection on the Notes tab, give it a name and add entries. They look and work like the daily log: tap the dot to tick, press and hold the dot for the type picker.
To put a task on a collection, press and hold its dot in the log and tap Collection. The same row takes it back to the daily log. Collections stay in bujo and are not written to Nextcloud.

title: Pick your paper font
bullets: Settings has a new Paper font choice: Newsreader, Literata, Source Serif or Lora. It sets the face of your titles, entries and day headings, and stays on this phone.
Journal text is a little heavier than before, so it reads more like pen on paper.
Quick entry now ends with two handwritten words: Done saves and closes, Next line saves and starts the next one. Enter still saves and closes.

title: The log follows your paper
bullets: Entries now sit in the order of the paper. A scanned page files its lines in page order, and anything you typed in the app and have not written down yet stays at the end of the day.

A long day can run over several pages. When a day already has paper, the scan asks which page the photo shows: pick an earlier page to rescan it, or the next one to continue the day. A rescan of page 1 never touches page 2.
Where a new page starts, a quiet dashed line with the page number sits in the log.

title: Mark what matters with a star
bullets: Hold the bullet of an entry and tap Important to put a handwritten * in the margin, just before the bullet. Tap it again to take it off.
A * in front of a bullet on a scanned page is read as important, and kept when you apply the scan.
In Nextcloud an important task is written with priority high. Without the star the priority is left alone.

title: One tap to close a task, hold for the type
bullets: Tap the bullet of a task to mark it done, and tap again to open it up. The tap target is bigger now.
Hold the bullet to pick any type: task, done, moved, scheduled, event or note. Moved and scheduled ask where the entry goes.
Hold the title or the rest of the row to select, as before.

title: Migrate your open tasks
bullets: When earlier days still hold open tasks, a quiet line on today's page offers to review them. "Review earlier tasks" is always at the foot of a daily page.
Go through them one at a time, oldest first: keep a task (it moves to today and leaves a > behind), schedule it (it leaves a <), or drop it (struck through, it stays where it was).
Keep all remaining moves the rest to today in one go. A short tally ends the review.

title: Swipe a task to move it
bullets: Swipe an open task to the right to move it (>), or to the left to schedule it (<). A chooser asks where it goes.
Let go early and the row snaps back, nothing changes. Tap the bullet to mark a task done.
Swiping empty paper still turns the page.

title: The month calendar is its own page
bullets: The Month calendar no longer shows your daily log. Daily entries stay on their day in the Daily view and are not copied onto the calendar.
The calendar has its own entries. A scanned calendar page now files onto the calendar, and no longer adds lines to the daily log.
Entries that were already in your daily log stay there, even if they came from an earlier calendar scan.

title: Scans forgive bad reading
bullets: A scanned line that is at least 70% like an item already on that day or page is now the same item. Reading slips no longer add a second copy.
The scan review shows each matched line with "matches: ..." and what applying will do to it, such as marking it done or migrated.
If a match is wrong, tap Not the same and the line becomes a new entry.

title: Month and Future like the paper
bullets: Month now opens on a calendar page: every day of the month on its own line, like "1 M", with the day's entries beside it. Days with nothing on them stay as empty lines.
The month's tasks have their own page. Turn from the calendar to the tasks, and on to the next month.
Future shows three months to a page, divided by thin lines, and a second page for the next three.

title: Quick fixes
bullets: Moving an entry with > to a day more than a week away now keeps it reachable: its day opens from the arrows and the calendar.
The > chooser has a Today option, shown when the entry is on another day.
The Time key opens the time picker on the first tap.
In the scan review each line has a Keep box with its word, so it is clear you can untick a line.
Picking a tag in the tag popup now closes it.

title: One sheet of paper
bullets: The Daily, Month and Future pages now scroll as one sheet: the title, the Future | Month | Daily switcher and the date move up with the rows and the dots.
The dots run in one piece from the top of the screen, and a page turn slides the whole page, header included.

title: Enter closes the sheet
bullets: Press Enter in the entry sheet to save the line and close the sheet. On an empty line it just closes.
To keep writing, tap + Next on the keyboard bar. It saves the line and opens a fresh one.

title: Scan more than a day
bullets: Scan a Future log, a calendar page or a month task list, not only a daily page. The app reads which kind it is, and you can change it in the review.
Future items go under their months, and calendar days go under their day. You can fix a month or a day on any line before you apply.
Scanned from the Future or Month view, the page is read as that kind first. After you apply, the log opens on where the lines landed.

title: Move entries between your logs
bullets: Set an entry to Moved (>) to carry it to the next day, a day you pick, this month or a later month. It keeps its place in your log and leaves a quiet > line on the page it came from.
Set an entry to Scheduled (<) to put it on a day or in a later month. Choose This day to keep it where it is.
The Future and Month views show what you moved there, and moves made offline are sent when you are back.

title: Dots that move with the page
bullets: The dotted grid now scrolls with your entries, so the page feels like paper under your pen.
The dots are quieter, and the words sit on a soft wash, so they no longer show through the letters.
Ink is a little darker and clearer, including tags, times and done lines, in light and dark.

title: Future and Month views
bullets: A switcher above the date now flips the log between Future, Month and Daily. Daily is still where it opens.
The Future Log looks six months ahead. The Month view lists the days of one month that have entries, plus tasks for the month itself.
Write @december, @dez or @12.2027 in an entry to file it under a whole month instead of a day.

title: A page that reads like handwriting
bullets: Entries no longer sit in outlined cards. They are written straight on the dotted page, one line to each grid row.
Tags and the time follow the title in a handwritten script, each tag in its own pen colour.
The day picker now opens in the middle of the screen, under the date.

title: One day per page
bullets: The Daily Log is now a notebook: each day is its own page. Swipe, tap the arrows or the page edges to turn it.
Tap the date to pick a day from a small calendar. Days with entries are marked.
On any other day, tap Today to jump back to the current page.

title: Pick the type from the marker
bullets: While you write an entry, tap the marker at the start of the line to choose its type: task, done, moved, scheduled, event or note.
The marker now looks tappable, and the Type key is gone from the bar above the keyboard.
It works offline too: the entry waits to send with the type you picked.

title: Tap to tick, and a calmer page
bullets: Tap the bullet of a task to mark it done, or swipe a row to the right. It works offline too.
The dot grid is quieter behind your words, and done entries no longer count as not on paper.
Rapid log is now called Daily log.

title: Write entries without a connection
bullets: New entries made offline wait on your phone, marked waiting to send, and go out by themselves when you are back online.
The log and Notes keep showing your last rows with a quiet offline note instead of an error.

title: Add an entry in one tap
bullets: Add in the centre of the bar opens a new entry at once, from any tab, with the keyboard ready.
Scan is now a camera button in the bottom bar, next to Add, and still opens the camera straight away.

title: Clearer rescans, fewer false marks
bullets: The rescan review now says Show 3 unchanged or Hide 3 unchanged, and its last line stays clear of the Apply button.
Not on paper only counts entries from the last 14 days, so old entries no longer all look unwritten.
Recent notes that are not on paper yet wear the same small page mark as the log.

title: See what is not on paper yet
bullets: Entries you made in the app carry a small page mark until you have written them in your journal.
Open Not on paper at the top of the log to copy them all, or mark each one as written.

title: Tabs that switch at once
bullets: Rapid log, Notes and Account now swap in place. The bar stays put and the page fades in.
A page you have seen before shows right away, with no loading flash, and updates quietly.

title: Copy entries as paper lines
bullets: Tap the copy key in the bar above the keyboard to copy the entry you are editing.
Press and hold an entry to select several, then copy them as paper lines, grouped by day.

title: Scan from the bottom bar
bullets: Scan now lives in the bottom bar and opens the camera straight away.
While a page is read you see the photo, a clear progress state and the elapsed time.

title: Tags and days that complete themselves
bullets: Type # or @ in an entry and suggestions appear above the keyboard: your own tags, or days like @morgen, @mo and @23.11.
An entry can carry several tags now, and the Tag key opens a search that finds a tag even when you type it roughly.

title: Settings on paper, and a theme choice
bullets: Settings, sign-in, Backlog and Scan now match the paper look of the rapid log.
You can pick System, Light or Dark in Settings. The choice stays on every page.

title: Longer titles, better Back
bullets: The title field in the edit sheet now wraps and grows, so a long entry is fully visible while you type.
On Android, one Back closes the keyboard and the entry together, and saves your change.

title: A home for your notes
bullets: Your notes have their own screen now, in a two-column grid with a photo and a title on each card.
Rapid log, Notes and Account sit in a bar at the bottom. The settings icon at the top right is gone.

title: Scan the same page again
bullets: Scan a page more than once in a day: lines already in your log are matched, not added twice.
The review shows only new lines and edits, with before and after. Nothing is ever deleted.

title: Cards drawn with a pen
bullets: Entries are now outlined in fine pen strokes, so the dotted paper shows through.
The edit sheet is inked too, with a hand-drawn top, handle and chips.

title: Back stays in the app
bullets: On Android, Back now closes the open sheet, scan view or page instead of leaving the app.
The icon bar now hides when the keyboard closes.

title: Soft paper cards
bullets: Each entry is now a card. Tags and times sit under the title as small pills.
Editing opens a sheet above the keyboard, with the icon bar at its foot.

title: Sharper handwriting scans
bullets: Pages are now read by an AI model.
The old reader is still there as a fallback.

title: Events sync to a test calendar
bullets: Rapid-log events are pushed to a Nextcloud test calendar (bujo-test-cal).

title: Tags, times and a slimmer bar
bullets: The bar above the keyboard is icons only: type, tag, date, time, delete, move and indent.
A written #tag or a time like 14:30 becomes a pill and is taken out of the title.

title: Scanned pages stay with your notes
bullets: The photo of a scanned page is saved with its markdown note.
Tap the thumbnail in a note to open the photo full size.

title: Type entries right in the log
bullets: Entries are one-line rows now.
A small bar above the keyboard has Type, Tag, Date and Time.
Type like in a text document. There is no big new-entry popup.

title: Free notes as markdown
bullets: A free note is saved as markdown in the app, with a Copy button.
Notes no longer show a not-synced label or a sync dot. They stay in the log and are not part of the task-list sync.

title: Scan from your gallery
bullets: The scan camera can pick a photo from your gallery, not only a live shot.
